title: Ethiopian Beef Tendons Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the whole-animal collagen stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Jimat Wat — beef tendons slow-cooked for 2.5 hours in a berbere-kibbeh sauce until the collagen converts completely to a rich, sticky, deeply gelatinous stew. The whole-animal dish that produces the most extraordinarily textured sauce in Ethiopian cooking.
longDesc: Jimat Wat requires patience — 2.5 hours of simmering converts the tough tendon collagen completely to gelatin, producing a stew so rich and sticky it coats the injera magnificently. It is the dish of those who know their Ethiopian cooking deeply.
ingredients: 600g beef tendons — cleaned, cut into sections
steps: Blanch tendons 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Add kibbeh and berbere. Toast 3 minutes.
Add water. Simmer covered on lowest heat 2—2.5 hours.
The sauce will become deeply gelatinous and thick.
Pressure cooker: 45 minutes reduces cooking time dramatically.
chefTips: Patience is the entire recipe — the tendons need 2.5 hours.
Pressure cooker dramatically reduces cooking time.
The stickiness of the sauce is the quality indicator.
cookingScience: Tendons are almost pure collagen — over 90% protein, with minimal fat and no muscle fibre. At 90°C over extended cooking time, the collagen triple-helix structure uncoils into gelatin chains, producing the characteristically thick, sticky, adhesive sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Tendons are typically discarded — this dish is the ultimate whole-animal use.
culturalNote: Jimat Wat is the dish of the dedicated Ethiopian cook — hours of patience producing a sauce of extraordinary texture. Those who know it, love it deeply.
